evals.prompt: We need to build a GitHub webhook intake service for our internal automation stack. It should receive webhook events, validate signatures, normalize payloads, persist raw deliveries, emit internal events for downstream workers, and expose a small admin replay endpoint. Produce the technical specs engineers and AI coders need to build this properly. The why is already settled in our tracker issue; do not re-narrate it.
evals.expected_output: A minimal three-genre set: an Interface doc (webhook contract + replay endpoint: validation groups, parameter tables, no secrets), a Process spec (definition opener, stage-named sections with trigger-first bullets, failure raised in-stage as events, per-mechanism verification lists), and a Data page (delivery table schema, event catalog with ID grammar, key/queue inventory with TTLs). No PRD (why exists upstream), no README (under three files is fine), identifiers literal and shared across the three docs, no section filled without decision content.

evals.prompt: I have a rough feature idea for a document ingestion platform: upload files, normalize metadata, extract text asynchronously, store artifacts, and make downstream search indexing easy. Break the design into the right specs with the data flow clear first and the APIs and data structures nailed down, clean enough to map to separate implementation tasks.
evals.expected_output: Identifier system and Data surfaces designed first (schemas, artifact keys, queue roster, event IDs); Interface doc for the upload/query contracts; one Process spec per bounded mechanism (upload processing, async extraction worker) each closing with testable verification lists; features cut so each Process unit plus its Interface/Data deltas maps to one implementation task; variants and shared behavior expressed as deltas, never cloned; deletion-pass economy throughout.

evals.prompt: Design the specs for a fraud-throttle subsystem for our payments platform. Events come in from transaction streams, risk counters are updated by merchant and region, temporary limit state is written to cache, downstream workers are notified, and operators need to know how to inspect and use the subsystem. The product why is still fuzzy.
evals.expected_output: A compact PRD written first (no upstream why exists), then the three-genre set: Data (counter key grammar with literal separators and TTLs, notification channels, event ID families), Process (stream-consumer stage sections with thresholds and failure-in-place, circuit-breaker as its own mechanism section), Interface (operator-facing inspection surface / manual). Rationale limited to single clauses; verification lists per unit; no generic failure/observability sections; no restatement between sibling docs.
